name: PinkPantheress
label: Warner Records
lede: She posted a song a day because she had nothing else to do, and four years later a mixtape with a crown on the cover landed on the year-end lists.

eras.title: A song a day, nothing else to do
eras.text: A university student in Kent posts loops on TikTok, two go viral, and two labels sign her within months. The mixtape follows.

years.h: PinkPantheress posts day 11 of a song a day, and "Pain" takes off
years.p: A student in Kent records a song an hour after class and posts 20-second loops to TikTok. The 12-second "Pain" clip is the one that catches.
years.xp:
Victoria Walker, then studying film at University of the Arts London, posted the "Pain" snippet in January 2021 with the caption "Day 11 of posting a song every day bc i have nothing else to do." It built on a sample of Sweet Female Attitude's 2000 garage hit "Flowers" and a piano loop based on Erik Satie's "Trois Gymnopédies".

She made it herself, and the full song runs 1:38. The full song came out on June 7, 2021, peaked at No. 35 in the UK and later went platinum there; Pitchfork ranked it No. 90 on its 2024 list of the 100 best songs of the 2020s so far.

years.h: Parlophone signs her in April, and Elektra follows in June
years.p: The TikTok bedroom producer has two label deals about two months apart, and her first mixtape comes out on both that October.

years.h: "Just for Me" takes four hours in a studio with [[Mura Masa|d2a76e1b-cecc-4500-b445-d55591821cd3]]
years.p: The song about an unhealthy crush reaches No. 27 in the UK and gets two million TikTok videos.
years.xp:
PinkPantheress cited Eminem's "Stan" and a wish to sound like Craig David as starting points. Mura Masa produced and played drums and keyboards, and the pair cut it in a four-hour session about two weeks before release.

[[Central Cee|b0337af1-8d93-4671-b6c9-ba306bf942bf]] later sampled it heavily for "Obsessed with You", and Giveon and Coldplay both covered it for BBC Live Lounge.

years.cap: PinkPantheress around the release of To Hell with It, October 2021
years.h: To Hell with It fits jungle, garage and pop-punk into 18 minutes
years.p: The debut mixtape runs 18 minutes 36 seconds and debuts at No. 20 in the UK. Mura Masa, Adam F and Oscar Scheller are among the producers.
years.xp:
It samples Sweet Female Attitude, Crystal Waters' "Gypsy Woman" and Linkin Park's "Forgotten". Pitchfork gave it 7.3 and called her vocals strangely soothing; Metacritic lists it at 86.

The cover, shot by Brent McKeever, has her outside a mansion at night with lightning behind her.

eras.title: Sound of 2022, and a quieter ear
eras.text: The BBC crowns her, and a hearing problem forces her off a festival bill.

years.h: The BBC names her Sound of 2022
years.p: She wins the tastemaker poll with a handful of singles and one mixtape behind her.

years.h: She cancels Primavera Sound in Barcelona over hearing loss
years.p: She became about 80% deaf in her right ear in 2022 after microphone feedback.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the hearing problem began as tinnitus from microphone feedback, and that voices sound to her mostly like bass. Her Primavera Sound Barcelona set that June was the date she pulled.

eras.title: Boy's a Liar, and a first album
eras.text: A remix with Ice Spice makes her a transatlantic pop name, and Heaven Knows follows.

years.h: Ice Spice joins, and "Boy's a Liar Pt. 2" gives both of them a first top ten
years.p: It debuts at No. 14 on the Billboard Hot 100, then climbs to No. 3.
years.xp:
[[Ice Spice|6f2c949d-9540-4421-bf02-27ae27e00e33]] had posted her own version on Instagram; PinkPantheress reached out with the idea of "stamping" the song into 2023 and rebuilt it from Mura Masa's instrumental stems. The video, by George and Frederick Buford, was shot in mid-January 2023 around New York: Harlem rooftops, fire escapes and subway cars.

It peaked at No. 2 in Canada and No. 1 in New Zealand, and went platinum in the US. Several outlets called its absence from the 2024 Grammy nominations a snub.

years.h: Pitchfork gives Heaven Knows 6.4 and Clash gives it 9
years.p: Her first album has [[Central Cee|b0337af1-8d93-4671-b6c9-ba306bf942bf]], Rema and Kelela as guests, and Mura Masa and Greg Kurstin producing.
years.xp: It peaked at No. 28 in the UK and No. 61 on the Billboard 200, and Metacritic sits at 80 from 15 critics. Rolling Stone ranked it No. 64 on its best albums of 2023. Singles were "Boy's a Liar Pt. 2", "Mosquito", "Capable of Love" and "Nice to Meet You" with [[Central Cee|b0337af1-8d93-4671-b6c9-ba306bf942bf]].

eras.title: The pause
eras.text: She tours behind Olivia Rodrigo, then pulls the rest of her dates for health reasons.

years.h: She pulls her remaining August shows, citing health
years.p: She had been opening on Olivia Rodrigo's Guts tour that summer. The cancellation covers all of her remaining live dates in August.

eras.title: Fancy That
eras.text: A mixtape of big-beat, jungle and garage pop lands on year-end lists, and the awards follow.

years.h: "Tonight" borrows its strings from a Panic! at the Disco song
years.p: The lead single for Fancy That lifts the orchestral strings from "Do You Know What I'm Seeing?" and arrives with a Regency costume video.
years.xp:
Brendon Urie, Ryan Ross, Spencer Smith and Jon Walker get writing credits for the 2008 Panic! at the Disco original. Aksel Arvid and Count Baldor produced with PinkPantheress. Director Charlotte Rutherford took cues from Bridgerton and Jamiroquai's "King for a Day".

It reached No. 35 in the UK. Slant named it the best song of 2025, per Wikipedia.

years.h: "Stateside" flips Adina Howard and Groove Armada
years.p: She called it her favorite song on Fancy That, and it went to No. 3 in the UK.
years.xp: It samples Adina Howard's 1995 "Freak like Me" and Groove Armada's 1999 "I See You Baby". Aksel Arvid, Harrison Patrick Smith, Jkarri and PinkPantheress produced. The [[Zara Larsson|134e6410-6954-45d1-bd4a-0f2d2ad5471d]] remix, released October 10, hit No. 6 on the Hot 100 and topped the Billboard Global 200.

years.cap: PinkPantheress at a fan meet-up in London, May 2025
years.src: Wikipedia: Fancy That · Metacritic: Fancy That critic reviews
years.h: Fancy That debuts at No. 3 in the UK, her best showing at home
years.p: Pitchfork gives it 8.0 and ranks it No. 18 of 2025.
years.xp:
Harry Tafoya's Pitchfork review scored it 8.0; Metacritic lists it at 82 from 11 critics, all positive, with Variety at 92 and DIY at 100. It leans on Basement Jaxx, Groove Armada and Fatboy Slim, and 11,126 first-week UK units got it to No. 3.

She described the cover, with her in the Imperial State Crown among flowers, as everything kitsch and UK-centric. It also placed No. 7 on Billboard's year-end list.

years.big: "Takes me right back to where I started with music."
years.h: "Illegal" flips Underworld and starts a handshake trend
years.p: PinkPantheress on "Illegal", which samples "Dark & Long (Dark Train)" and reaches No. 22 in the UK.
years.xp: She also called the song's garage "gritty". Ethan & Tom directed the video, and it became her second Hot 100 entry, at No. 96.

years.h: Kylie Minogue, Sugababes and Basement Jaxx crowd onto Fancy Some More?
years.p: Seventeen, Anitta and Bladee also remix or join across three discs and 92 minutes. Pitchfork gives it 7.6.
years.xp: Disc three reissues the original mixtape whole. The project reached No. 30 on the Billboard 200 and No. 1 on Top Dance Albums. Pitchfork asked who else would have the cheek to gather all these people under one roof.

years.p: "Illegal" is up for Best Dance Pop Recording, and the mixtape for Best Dance/Electronic Album.

years.cap: PinkPantheress performing at Southside Ballroom, Dallas, April 2026
years.h: She wins British Producer of the Year at the Brit Awards
years.p: She is the youngest winner and the first woman to take it.
